review.limitations: Full chapters, formal proofs, painting specifications and aesthetic-system examples were not accessible in this review. This is a guide to the stated research program, not a verified summary of the whole book.

sections.title: What the book sets out to do
sections.text: Develop shape grammars through both visual and formal accounts, then connect generative descriptions of paintings with algorithmic approaches to criticism and design.

sections.title: The stated premise
sections.text: Definitions should be visually persuasive while supporting productive formal reasoning. The pictorial account studies shapes, relations and generation; the formal counterpart treats languages of two-dimensional rectilinear shapes.

sections.title: How the project is organized
sections.text: A visual introduction precedes a mathematical development requiring formal-language and automata knowledge. Later chapters introduce generative specifications of paintings, define aesthetic systems, and combine them with criticism and design algorithms.

sections.title: What the accessible material does not show
sections.text: The abstracts describe the project’s architecture but do not expose enough detail to check its proofs, algorithms or concrete examples. In particular, no computational-universality result is asserted here from a chapter heading alone.

sections.title: A useful route into the original
sections.text: Begin with the pictorial model for intuition; follow the formal model to inspect definitions and assumptions. Then ask how the painting specifications and aesthetic system depend on those choices.
